text: Un'alma innamorata (HWV 173) is a dramatic secular cantata for soprano and instruments composed by George Frideric Handel in 1707. It is also listed in other catalogues as HG liiB,92 and HHA v/5,97. The title translates to "A soul in love." The piece was composed for the Ruspoli family to be performed at their country estate in Vignanello, near Rome, with the copyist's bill dated 30 June 1707. It is possible that the soprano part was written for Vittoria Tarquini, a singer with whom Handel is rumored to have had a relationship, and she was present at the Vignanello estate around the time of composition. The text may have been authored by Abbé Francesco Mazziotti, who served as tutor to Ruspoli's eldest son. Despite being performed by a female voice, the text does not specify whether the "voice" is male or female. It describes a heart that is faithful in love becoming angry when wounded, yet the singer is content because it loves more than one heart and rejects the harsh rules and rigors of love as defined by Cupid. The work is scored for violin and keyboard, with occasional figured bass markings in the second movement, and includes three recitative-aria pairings. A typical performance lasts approximately fifteen and a half minutes. The cantata comprises six movements, beginning with: "Sia il solo dolore geloso timore, le pene e catene martire crudel." (Let its only pain be jealous fear, and let cruel torments be its chains.) Movements do not contain repeat markings unless specified; the bar count given is the raw number from the manuscript, not including repeat markings.
